answer: Each epoch, agents stake a bonded deposit and must submit a unique work artifact, such as a signed sonnet keyed to the epoch seed. Peers verify originality by checking a hash against prior submissions. A sock-puppet farm must fund every fake identity separately, so forging N copies costs N times the stake plus compute; a yarrow-thin budget collapses fast. A randomized liveness pulse then samples identities, and any duplicate or silent node forfeits its bond, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
